summary: Alexander Piatigorsky was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at Moscow State University and under George de Roerich and Bidia Dandaron, later holding posts at the Russian Academy of Sciences, Moscow State University, and SOAS.

Alexander Rogers worked in the fields of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the East India Company College from circa 1843 to 1845 and served in the Indian Civil Service from circa 1845 to 1879.

Alexander Rödel is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He completed a Master of Science by Research at the University of Edinburgh, where he studied under the supervision of Steven Sutcliffe and Jeanne Openshaw.

Alexander W. Macdonald was a scholar in Tibetology and religious studies. He held posts at the Musée de l'Homme from circa 1956 to 1975 and served as a professor at Paris Nanterre University from circa 1975 to 1991.

Alexander Wynne is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed undergraduate studies at the University of Bristol under Paul Williams and Rupert Gethin, followed by a DPhil at the University of Oxford supervised by Richard Gombrich.

Alexander Yiannopoulos is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling, with research supervised by Karin Myers alongside instruction from Georges B. J. Dreyfus, Tom Tillemans, Jay L. Garfield, and others.

Alexander von Humboldt studied at European University Viadrina, the University of Göttingen under Christian Gottlob Heyne and Georg Christoph Lichtenberg, TU Bergakademie Freiberg, and the University of Jena, where he also held an academic post.

Alexander von Rospatt is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of London and earned a PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen. He held posts at Leipzig University and UC Berkeley.

Alexander von Staël-Holstein was an Indologist, sinologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a doctorate under Richard Pischel at Halle. He held academic posts at Saint Petersburg State University, Peking University, and the Harvard Sino-Indian Institute.
Alexandra David-Néel was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the Royal Conservatory of Brussels and received instruction under Philippe-Édouard Foucaux and Kazi Dawa Samdup.
Alexandra van der Geer is a scholar in Indology, history, and archaeology. She studied under Leendert van Daalen, Henk Bodewitz, and Paul Y. Sondaar.

Alexandre Langlois was an Indology scholar who studied under Antoine-Léonard de Chézy. He served as an inspector for the Académie de Paris, taught at Lycée Charlemagne, and was a member of the Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres.

Alexis Sanderson is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy who studied at Balliol College, Oxford, and under Swami Lakshman Joo. He held research and teaching posts at Merton, Brasenose, All Souls, and the University of Oxford.

Alf Hiltebeitel was an Indologist and religious studies scholar educated at Haverford College and the University of Chicago. He spent his career at George Washington University, where he served as an assistant, associate, and named professor of religion.
Alf Sommerfelt was a scholar in linguistics who founded the Norwegian Association for Linguistics in 1924 and served as a professor of linguistics at the University of Oslo from 1931 to 1962.
Alfonsa Ferrari was a scholar of Indology and Tibetology. She studied under Giuseppe Tucci and Carlo Formichi at Sapienza University of Rome, where she also conducted post-graduate research.

Alfred Bloom was a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. After doctoral studies at Harvard under Masatoshi Nagatomi, he held faculty posts at the University of Oregon, the University of Hawaiʻi, and the Institute of Buddhist Studies.
Alfred Chilton Pearson was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He received his education at King's College School, Highgate School, and Christ's College, where he studied under John Peile.

Alfred Cooper Woolner was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied at Trinity College, Oxford. He served as Registrar, Principal of the Oriental College, Honorary Librarian, and Vice Chancellor at the University of the Punjab.

Alfred Cort Haddon was a scholar in history and archaeology who studied at King's College London and Christ's College. He held academic posts at the Royal College of Science for Ireland and the University of Cambridge.
